title: Inject commitment opening material (SECRET until reveal)
description: The withheld half of the commit/reveal pair. Held by Exercise Assurance. Publishing any part of this before the reveal trigger destroys the hiding property and voids the exercise's blind-inject design.

HANDLING.storage: EA-controlled secret manager or sealed offline medium. Never in the exercise channel, never in the shared evidence store before reveal.
HANDLING.access: Exercise Assurance only. Not White. Not any participant.
HANDLING.backup: MANDATORY. Loss of opening_salt makes the commitment permanently unopenable, which is indistinguishable from refusal to reveal.
HANDLING.destruction: Retained as evidence AFTER reveal (verification step 12). Do not destroy - it is what proves the commitment was honoured.

commitment_id.description: Links to the public commitment object.

opening_salt.description: 32 or 48 cryptographically random bytes, hex or base64. CSPRNG. NEVER REUSED across commitments.

salt_generation.reuse: PROHIBITED. Maintain a salt registry so verification step 11 (salt has not appeared in another commitment) is answerable.
salt_generation.why_secret: Randomness added to a hash defeats precomputation or enumeration ONLY when the attacker does not already know that randomness. A published nonce provides uniqueness, not hiding. Inject packages are short and structurally predictable, so an unhidden commitment is enumerable in practice.
